findings.text: Invest into an unlisted provider takes the reserve below the minimum ratio
Rebalance reverts when the prepared withdrawal exceeds the shortfall
Operators can still invest in a provider that the owner removed

A provider with an old storage namespace skips initialize: Code smells: `isInitialized` is read from diamond storage by delegatecall; `removeProvider` does not clear provider storage — An upgraded or re-added provider that uses the same storage namespace skips `initialize`, so `addProvider` ignores the new params. We did not check any provider storage layou

delegateBySelf delegatecalls any address with only a self-call guard: Code smells: public non-view function; only guard is `msg.sender == address(this)`; no `isProvider(providerAddress)` check; any `callData` — Any facet that makes the diamond call itself with user calldata gives that user a delegatecall to any address. We found no such facet in scope.

Disabling a funded pool hides its tokens and blocks withdrawal: Code smells: no zero-balance check; every withdraw path, `emergencyWithdraw` included, requires `onlyAssetPoolEnabled` — The owner can disable a pool that holds tokens, so the total drops and no operator can withdraw them until the owner enables it again.

Two providers can report one position twice: Code smells: providers run by delegatecall, so each `getAssetBalance` reads balances that the diamond holds; nothing separates the positions of two providers — If two providers read the same storage or receipt token, the total counts it twice and `invest` allows too much. Provider code is out of sco

The total leaves out funds in removed providers and disabled pools: Code smells: the loop reads only `ds.providers`; `getAssetBalance` returns 0 for a disabled pool; neither `removeProvider` nor `disableAssetPoolsForProvider` checks for a zero balance — The reserve limits use a total that omits tokens still held by providers. The path to a loss needs an owner action

One reverting provider blocks invest and rebalance for the asset: Code smells: the loop makes a static call to every provider, and one revert stops the whole sum — One provider whose `getAssetBalance` reverts makes `invest` and `rebalance` fail for every provider of that token. The owner can remove the provider to recover.

Rebalance has no role check, but only operators can complete it: Code smells: `rebalance` is external with no modifier; it calls the public `onlyOperator` functions `invest`, `directlyWithdraw`, `finishWithdrawal` and `prepareWithdrawal`, and they check the external `msg.sender` — A keeper that is not an operator gets a revert on every branch that moves tokens. Rebalance asks one provider for the full shortfall: Code smells: `amount = investmentReserve - remainingBalance` uses the total of all providers, and nothing caps it at `getAssetBalance(providerAddress, asset)` — With several providers, `rebalance` asks one provider for more than it holds, so the provider can revert. Reinvest takes any amount with no reserve check: Code smells: `reinvest(provider, asset, amount)` has no `minimumReserveRatio` check, while `invest` has one — An operator can move more than the reserve allows through `reinvest`. We did not confirm whether providers take `amount` from the idle balance of the diamond.
